title: Functions & Scope
description: Reusable blocks of code, inputs, return values, and who can see a variable.

screens.heading: A named recipe
screens.body:
A function is a named chunk of code you can run whenever you need it. You write the steps once. Then you call the name.

That is how you stop copying the same five lines into ten places.

code.snippet:
def greet():
    print("Hi, learner.")

greet()
greet()

screens.keyPoint: def names a function. The name plus () runs it.

screens.heading: Inputs are parameters
screens.body:
Most functions need a little information. Those inputs are parameters — empty labeled slots in the definition.

When you call the function, you pass arguments that fill those slots.

code.snippet:
def greet(name):
    print("Hi, " + name + ".")

greet("Sam")
greet("Byte")

screens.keyPoint: Parameters are the slots. Arguments are the values you pass in.

screens.heading: Give something back
screens.body:
print shows a value on the screen. return hands a value back to whoever called the function so you can store it or use it later.

If you forget return, Python gives back None. The function still ran — it just had nothing to hand over.

code.snippet:
def double(n):
    return n * 2

result = double(5)
print(result)

screens.keyPoint: return sends a value out. print only displays it.

screens.heading: Scope is who can see a name
screens.body:
A variable created inside a function lives only inside that function. Code outside cannot read it. That private space is local scope.

A variable created outside functions is global — functions can read it, but it is easier to pass values in as parameters than to lean on globals.

code.snippet:
def demo():
    secret = 7
    print(secret)

demo()
# print(secret)  # this would fail — secret is local

screens.keyPoint: Names created inside a function stay inside that function.

screens.heading: Why this matters
screens.body:
Small functions with clear inputs and a return value are easier to test, reuse, and explain. If a function does one job, you can understand it in one glance.

When you get stuck, ask: what goes in, what comes out, and which names exist only inside?
screens.keyPoint: One job per function. Pass data in, return data out.
